"executive_summary": "This study evaluated the combined effects of plant growth regulators (PGR) and nitrogen fertilization methods on the germination, growth, and physiological composition of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk. Experiments were conducted using coated and conventional seeds treated with varying levels of PGR (auxin, cytokinin, and gibberellin) and subjected to different nitrogen fertilization regimes (no fertilization, soil, foliar, or multiple). Results indicated that PGR application significantly increased germination percentages and root dry mass, with optimal levels varying by seed type (10.3 mL.kg⁻¹ for germination, 12.8 mL.kg⁻¹ for root mass). Coated seeds generally outperformed conventional seeds, particularly at lower PGR concentrations, suggesting higher embryo quality. Nitrogen fertilization, specifically soil application, was the most effective method for increasing dry matter yields of leaves, stems, shoots, and roots. The combination of PGR and soil fertilization yielded the highest biomass production, attributed to enhanced photosynthetic processes driven by increased chlorophyll a content. Conversely, multiple fertilization (soil + foliar) reduced leaf and stem production when combined with PGR, though it uniquely increased root mass. The study concludes that lower PGR levels are recommended for coated seeds, while soil nitrogen fertilization is critical for maximizing pasture establishment and structural development.",

summary.title: Influence of plant growth regulators and nitrogen sources on the production and development of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk
summary.authors: Leone Campos Rocha; Fábio Andrade; Teixeira; Márcio Dos Santos Pedreira; Daniela Deitos Fries; Giovanna Evely Leite Costa; Ana Cláudia Maia Soares; Daniel Lucas Santos Dias; Abdias José De Figueiredo; Angel Amaral Seixas; Camile Carvalho Pacheco
summary.executive_summary: This study evaluated the combined effects of plant growth regulators (PGR) and nitrogen fertilization methods on the germination, growth, and physiological composition of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk. Experiments were conducted using coated and conventional seeds treated with varying levels of PGR (auxin, cytokinin, and gibberellin) and subjected to different nitrogen fertilization regimes (no fertilization, soil, foliar, or multiple). Results indicated that PGR application significantly increased germination percentages and root dry mass, with optimal levels varying by seed type (10.3 mL.kg⁻¹ for germination, 12.8 mL.kg⁻¹ for root mass). Coated seeds generally outperformed conventional seeds, particularly at lower PGR concentrations, suggesting higher embryo quality. Nitrogen fertilization, specifically soil application, was the most effective method for increasing dry matter yields of leaves, stems, shoots, and roots. The combination of PGR and soil fertilization yielded the highest biomass production, attributed to enhanced photosynthetic processes driven by increased chlorophyll a content. Conversely, multiple fertilization (soil + foliar) reduced leaf and stem production when combined with PGR, though it uniquely increased root mass. The study concludes that lower PGR levels are recommended for coated seeds, while soil nitrogen fertilization is critical for maximizing pasture establishment and structural development.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study evaluated the combined effects of plant growth regulators (PGR) and nitrogen fertilization methods on the germination, growth, and physiological composition of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk. Experiments were conducted using coated and conventional seeds treated with varying levels of PGR (auxin, cytokinin, and gibberellin) and subjected to different nitrogen fertilization regimes (no fertilization, soil, foliar, or multiple). Results indicated that PGR application significantly increased germination percentages and root dry mass, with optimal levels varying by seed type (10.3 mL.kg⁻¹ for germination, 12.8 mL.kg⁻¹ for root mass). Coated seeds generally outperformed conventional seeds, particularly at lower PGR concentrations, suggesting higher embryo quality. Nitrogen fertilization, specifically soil application, was the most effective method for increasing dry matter yields of leaves, stems, shoots, and roots. The combination of PGR and soil fertilization yielded the highest biomass production, attributed to enhanced photosynthetic processes driven by increased chlorophyll a content. Conversely, multiple fertilization (soil + foliar) reduced leaf and stem production when combined with PGR, though it uniquely increased root mass. The study concludes that lower PGR levels are recommended for coated seeds, while soil nitrogen fertilization is critical for maximizing pasture establishment and structural development.

Research Context
Adverse climatic factors shorten the soil preparation and planting window. Greater seed efficiency is necessary for recovering degraded pastures. Phytohormones regulate homeostasis and activate genes for plant responses. PGRs act on signaling networks to activate genes and plant responses. High levels of gibberellin are uneconomical and reduce forage mass. Low concentrations of gibberellin positively affect forage yield. PGRs improve water use and mechanical impedance in dry soils. Nitrogen expands plant lifecycle and increases growth rates. Nitrogen increases rates of cell division and expansion.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aimed to evaluate PGR and nitrogen effects on growth and development. Hypothesis: PGRs increase germination and mass yields of plant structures. Hypothesis: Optimal PGR levels differ for germination versus root mass. Hypothesis: Seed type interacts with PGR levels for leaf and pseudostem mass. Hypothesis: Coated seeds perform better with absence or lower levels of PGR. Hypothesis: Soil N-fertilization increases dry mass production of all structures. Hypothesis: PGR and soil fertilization maximize photoassimilate rates. Hypothesis: Exogenous hormones act on organogenesis of plant tissues.

Methodological Details
Experiments were performed at UESB, Itapetinga -BA between June and September 2017. Germination was carried out under a 12h photoperiod and at constant temperature (28ºC). Each pot was filled with eight liters or 12 kg of dry soil. Soil was collected at 0-20 cm depth and passed through a 4-mm sieve. A 2 x 4 factorial scheme was used in a completely randomized design (CRD). Two commercial seed types (coated and conventional) were used. Four levels of growth regulator were 0, 8, 16, 24 mL.kg -1 of seed. The PGR was composed of auxin (0.05 mg.L -1 ), cytokinin (0.09 mg.L -1 ) and gibberellin (0.05 mg.L -1 ). Seeds were wrapped in filter paper moistened with distilled water. Initial growth assessments used 25 seeds per replicate and four replicates per treatment. Substrate for initial growth was sterilized coconut residue. Exp 2 evaluated four nitrogen fertilization methods: no, soil, foliar, and multiple. Fertilization recommendations were 75 kg.ha -1 N for soil and 3 L.ha -1 for foliar. Data were analyzed using the MIXED procedure of SAS. Significance was declared when P ≤ 0.05.

Procedures And Architectures
Germination was evaluated daily for 14 days to determine percentage and GSI. Whole-plant yield was determined followed by desiccation of root, stem and leaf. Chlorophylls were quantified by absorption spectrophotometry at 665, 649 and 480 nm. Leaves were cut and an aliquot of 200 mg of fresh mass was prepared. Values were adjusted to mg.g -1 of fresh mass. A standardization cut was performed adopting an average residue height of 15 cm. Data collection started after the standardization cut. Fertilization was performed after the standardization cut. The composition of the foliar fertilizer is described in Table 1. Single-degree-of-freedom contrast statements were constructed to analyze PGR effects. The maximum point was estimated from a regression equation. Tukey test was used as a comparison of means.

Key Results
Interaction between seed type and PGR was not significant for germination. Quadratic effect of PGR levels on germination was observed regardless of seed type. Treatment with 10.3 mL.kg -1 promotes greater germination. Coated seeds had higher values for germination and GSI. Treatment with 12.8 mL.kg -1 resulted in higher root dry mass production. Interaction between seed type and PGR was significant for leaf and pseudostem mass. Higher leaf and pseudostem mass was observed at 8.85 and 9.57 mL.kg -1. Conventional seeds required 15.5 and 18.1 mL.kg -1 for leaf and pseudostem mass. Interaction between PGR and nitrogen fertilization was significant for dry mass production. Soil fertilization resulted in higher yields regardless of PGR. PGR reduced leaf, stem, and shoot production when combined with multiple fertilization. PGR increased root dry mass production only when combined with multiple fertilization. Interaction between PGR and nitrogen was not significant for chlorophyll contents. There was a significant effect for the use of PGR on chlorophyll a. Fertilization methods influenced the levels of chlorophyll a, b and carotenoids.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Exogenous hormone compounds change hormonal balance and biosynthesis levels. Gibberellin increases germination by reducing abscisic acid concentrations. Coated seeds had higher germination due to quality and protection. Seed coating provides protection against mechanical damage and nutrients. Auxin in the composition increases rhizogenesis. Auxin stimulates stem cell multiplication in quiescent centers. Conventional seeds required greater use of growth regulators due to reduced efficiency. Hormonal interaction is comprised of a signaling network. Soil fertilization justifies nitrogen relationship and greater efficiency. Nitrogen supply combined with PGR reflects in higher dry mass accumulation. Increased chlorophyll a promotes the formation of ATP in photophosphorylation. Foliar fertilization allows faster access to nitrogen by growing plant tissues.

Contradictions And Limitations
Little is known about the role of auxins and cytokinins in photosynthetic processes. Auxin may indirectly influence the movement of chloroplasts. Growth regulators in herbicide form act by blocking photosynthetic electron flux. No influence of foliar fertilization was observed when used exclusively.

Claims
Lower levels of PGR are recommended for coated seeds compared to conventional methods. Coated seeds had greater performance with absence or at lower levels of growth regulators. Best responses observed in the combination of coated seeds and lower levels. Conventional seeds required higher levels of the treatment for leaf and pseudostem dry mass production. Lower levels of PGR were recommended in coated seeds when compared to conventional methods.
Soil N-fertilization promotes an increase in mass yield and chlorophyll content. Soil N-fertilization resulted in higher dry mass productions of leaf, stem, shoot and root. The use of fertilization methods influenced the levels of chlorophyll a, b and carotenoids. No influence of foliar fertilization was observed when used exclusively. Soil N-fertilization increase mass yields as it maximizes photosynthetic processes and growth rates.

Data And Code Availability
Data were analyzed using the MIXED procedure of SAS.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Single-degree-of-freedom contrast statements were constructed to analyze PGR effects. The maximum point was estimated from a regression equation.

Key Figures Tables
Fig 1 shows the average, minimum and maximum temperatures and relative humidity. Table 1 describes the composition of foliar spray. Table 2 shows the difference for seed type for germination and GSI. Table 3 shows the root dry mass production based on the estimated equation. Table 4 shows the leaf and pseudostem dry mass production for different seed types. Table 5 shows the interaction between PGR and nitrogen fertilization methods. Table 6 shows the contents of chlorophyll a, b and carotenoids.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is that PGRs increase germination and mass yields. 2. The strongest evidence is the significant interaction between seed type and PGR for leaf and pseudostem mass. 3. The future path involves evaluating Pure Live Seeds (PLS) to improve hormone use efficiency.
